sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: A YAML file describing the multi-container app (app + DB + cache): services, ports, env vars, depends_on, volumes. docker compose up — the whole stack, networked. The local environment that mirrors prod.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The compose file for a Go service + PostgreSQL:

```yaml
version: "3.9"
services:
  app:
    build: .                    # build from the Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"            # host:container
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://db:5432/app?sslmode=disable
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - ./:/app                 # dev: live-reload the source

  db:
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
      POSTGRES_DB: app
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
      interval: 5s
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  pgdata:                        # named volume — the DB survives restarts
```

The commands:
```bash
docker compose up -d       # the whole stack, detached
docker compose logs -f app  # the app's output
docker compose down         # stop and remove
docker compose down -v     # also remove volumes (the DB)
```

The features interviewers probe:
- The NETWORK: compose creates a network where services reach each other by NAME (the app connects to db:5432 — the hostname IS the service name)
- depends_on + healthcheck: the app waits for the DB to be READY (not just started) — the startup-order problem solved
- The named volume (pgdata): the DB's data survives compose down (survives the container); -v deletes it
- The dev-mode volume mapping (./:/app): the host's source mounted in the container — Go's live-reload setups run on this

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[app service] --> B[build: Dockerfile]
    A --> P[ports: 8080:8080]
    A --> E[env: DATABASE_URL]
    A --> D[depends_on: db healthy]
    D --> DB[db service: postgres:16]
    DB --> V[volume: pgdata]
    A --> NET[compose network: app ↔ db by name]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The name-resolution mechanics: compose creates a bridge network; each service gets a DNS alias matching its name. The app's DATABASE_URL references db:5432 — the name resolves to the DB container's IP on the compose network. The same pattern in Kubernetes is the Service; in prod, the service discovery — compose is the local mirror.

The depends_on evolution: the simple form (depends_on: [db]) waits for the DB container to START — not for PostgreSQL to be READY to accept connections (the race: app connects to a starting DB, gets a connection refused). The healthcheck form (condition: service_healthy) solves it — the app's start waits until pg_isready succeeds. The production equivalent: readiness probes + init containers.

The volume types: named (pgdata — compose-managed, the data survives) vs bind (./:/app — the host directory mapped in, the dev-time live code). The volume lifecycle: down preserves named volumes; down -v removes — the dev-reset command for the database.
